The Lumpyr system introduces an operator written !. It combines two whole numbers and produces a whole number.
To evaluate x ! y, first compare. If y is at least x, the result is y plus 2. Otherwise the result is 7 times x.
Every result in this system is reduced modulo 1000. After computing a value, divide it by 1000 and keep only the remainder.

To evaluate x < y, subtract x from y, multiply that difference by 5, then add 5.
Every result in this system is reduced modulo 1000. After computing a value, divide it by 1000 and keep only the remainder.
When an expression contains more than one < and no parentheses, < associates right to left. Parentheses, where written, are evaluated first.
Worked example: 7 < 4 = 990.
Worked example: 12 < 5 = 970. <|doc|> The Zamovi System.

To evaluate x ~ y, first compare. If y is at least x, the result is y plus 10. Otherwise the result is 3 times x.
Every result in this system is reduced modulo 100. After computing a value, divide it by 100 and keep only the remainder.
When an expression contains more than one ~ and no parentheses, ~ associates right to left. Parentheses, where written, are evaluated first.
Worked example: 7 ~ 4 = 21.
Worked example: 12 ~ 5 = 36. <|doc|> The Zelbra System.

The Zelbra system introduces an operator written !. It combines two whole numbers and produces a whole number.
To evaluate x ! y, first compare. If y is at least x, the result is y plus 1. Otherwise the result is 2 times x.
Every result in this system is reduced modulo 100. After computing a value, divide it by 100 and keep only the remainder.
When an expression contains more than one ! and no parentheses, ! associates left to right. Parentheses, where written, are evaluated first.
Worked example: 7 ! 4 = 14.
Worked example: 12 ! 5 = 24. <|q|> Evaluate 3 ~ 12 ~ 3 ~ 2 ~ 11. <|a|>

The Zamka system introduces an operator written !. It combines two whole numbers and produces a whole number.
To evaluate x ! y, subtract x from y, multiply that difference by 5, then add 5.
Every result in this system is reduced modulo 1000. After computing a value, divide it by 1000 and keep only the remainder.
When an expression contains more than one ! and no parentheses, ! associates right to left. Parentheses, where written, are evaluated first.
Worked example: 7 ! 4 = 990.
Worked example: 12 ! 5 = 970. <|q|> Evaluate 7 ! 4 ! 8. <|a|>
